chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: Lester Young's influence from Frankie Trumbauer
summary: Collins notes Lester's debt to Trumbauer, which Lester confirmed, and traces the line to Getz and Al Cohn.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: I heard records of them, I didn't hear them in person. I heard Putney Dandridge, but these records, if you listen you'll see how much they contributed and how similar some of the things they're doing -- they were doing then are to the things that the guys are doing today. You know. And saxophone, like Lester Young was different, but he always reminded me of a guy that played with Paul Whiteman, Frankie Trombar. And then talking to him in later years he was influenced by Frankie Trumbauer, he told me. You know. And so now from Lester came Alan Eager, Stan Getz, all of these. So this is just an extension of what had been done. I'm taking you down the line now, you know, from Frankie Trumbauer, Lester, Stan Getz, and so forth. See, this is -- So they should really -- I mean go and listen to what is -- to some of the older musicians, what have been done before.
And did Lester mention any other influences besides Frankie Trombar?

No, he mentioned -- it was so -- I liked Frankie Trumbauer so much, myself, and I broached the subject to him because I saw the similarity. Because there was just a plain quality to Frankie Trumbauer's playing that always kind of grabbed me. Something a little different. And I recognized the same thing in Lester's playing. And finally I asked him and he told me that he was influenced by Frankie Trumbauer.
